Thick Chocolate Masa Champurrado

Served at: La Noche de Rabanos

Serves 4Prep 10 minCook 20 min

Champurrado is a traditional Mexican thick hot chocolate drink made with masa harina, enjoyed especially during festive occasions like La Noche de Rábanos (The Night of the Radishes) in Oaxaca. This warm, comforting beverage combines rich chocolate and corn masa, making it a beloved treat to accompany the holiday's vibrant celebrations.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (960 ml) whole milk
  • 1 cup (240 ml) water
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) masa harina (corn dough flour)
  • 3 oz (85 g) Mexican chocolate tablet or bittersweet chocolate, chopped
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 1 cinnamon stick
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • Pinch of salt

Method

  1. In a medium saucepan, combine the water and cinnamon stick and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
  2. In a separate bowl, whisk the masa harina with 1 cup (240 ml) of the milk until smooth and free of lumps.
  3. Slowly pour the masa mixture into the simmering water, whisking constantly to prevent lumps.
  4. Add the remaining milk to the saucepan and continue to whisk until the mixture thickens slightly, about 5 minutes.
  5. Add the chopped chocolate, sugar, and salt to the saucepan, stirring continuously until the chocolate and sugar have fully melted and the champurrado is thick and smooth, about 7-10 minutes.
  6. Remove the cinnamon stick and stir in the vanilla extract.
  7. Serve hot in mugs, perfect for enjoying during La Noche de Rábanos festivities.

Tips

  • Use Mexican chocolate like Abuelita or Ibarra for authentic flavor.
  • Adjust the thickness by adding more milk if too thick or more masa harina dissolved in milk if too thin.
  • For a dairy-free version, substitute milk with almond or oat milk.
